newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house telecom law vote seen Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house telecom law vote seen Wednesday.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies may vote Wednesday on a bill regulating Brazil's telecoms sector and outlining the privatization of the federal Telebras system, a congressional source said Monday.
"Nothing's been officially scheduled yet but it could be Wednesday," said a spokeswoman for Deputy Alberto Goldman, who drafted the bill.

Lower house leaders are expected to ask Tuesday that the bill containing the new General Telecommunications Law be considered a priority and placed on Wednesday's agenda for the Chamber of Deputies, she said.
"There's nothing definite yet. We'll see what happens tomorrow," the spokeswoman said.
The law, which authorizes the break-up and sale of Telebras lower house panel. If approved by deputies, the bill would be sent to the Senate for a final nod.
The committee made few changes in Goldman's draft bill, despite disagreement on foreign capital participation in telecom operators and the autonomy of a new regulator to oversee the sector.
Analysts expect debate in the lower house to focus on the independence of the watchdog entity as well as attempts by some deputies to require a limit on foreigners investing in Brazilian telecoms.
The bill approved by the committee places no restriction on foreigners but allows the executive branch to set limits on a case-by-case basis.
It also provides for the new National Telecommunications Agency (Antel) to have its own budget as a way of ensuring its independence from the government and Congress.
